```{r setup}
library(dplyr); library(readr); library(tidyr); library(stringr); library(knitr)
root <- normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), ".."))
op  <- function(...) file.path(root, "output", ...)
tb  <- function(...) file.path(root, "exports", "tables", ...)
fig <- function(...) file.path(root, "exports", "figures", ...)
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "catalog.R"))    # PERIOD_LEVELS / LABELS

national <- read_csv(op("kpi_national.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
master   <- read_csv(op("master_woreda.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
dq       <- read_csv(tb("trend_data_quality.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
part     <- read_csv(tb("trend_participation_by_period.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
comp_w   <- read_csv(tb("trend_region_composite_wide.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

periods <- intersect(PERIOD_LEVELS, unique(master$period))
plabs   <- ifelse(periods %in% names(PERIOD_LABELS), PERIOD_LABELS[periods], periods)
np <- length(periods)
```

## What this report compares

This companion to the single-period KPI report puts the **`r np` reporting
periods now in the database side by side** so we can see how reporting and
performance moved over 2025:

`r paste0("- **", plabs, "** (", periods, ")", collapse = "\n")`

The standing single-period report (`kpi_report.qmd`) still covers the newest
period on its own and is unchanged. This report adds the comparison.

> **One caveat governs every comparison here.** **Wk 28–52 spans two quarters**
> (weeks 28–52), while **Wk 3–15 and Wk 16–27 are each a single quarter.** The
> KPIs are **proportions** — ratios of a numerator to a denominator — so they are
> **directly comparable across periods regardless of length.** Only *raw counts*
> (woredas, cases, events) scale with period length, and those panels say so.

## Headline findings

```{r}
dqx <- dq |> arrange(match(period, periods))
ow  <- comp_w  # region composite wide
```

1. **The reporting base narrowed over the year.** Mapped woredas reporting fell
   from **`r dqx$mapped_woredas[1]`** in `r plabs[1]` to
   **`r dqx$mapped_woredas[np]`** in `r plabs[np]`. The number of regions
   reporting fell from **`r dqx$regions_reporting[1]`** to
   **`r dqx$regions_reporting[np]`**.
2. **Two regions reported only in the first period.** Tigray and Central
   Ethiopia submitted in Wk 3–15 and did not appear in either later period.
3. **Oromia and Harari coverage fell sharply.** Oromia reported
   **326 → 322 → 8** woredas across the three periods, and Harari reported
   **9 → 9 → 1**. Their later-period scores rest on a small number of units and
   should not be read as regional performance.
4. **Completeness of the returns that were submitted improved.** The share of
   indicator entries filled rose from **`r dqx$pct_filled[1]`%** to
   **`r dqx$pct_filled[np]`%**. ("Indicator entries filled" is the share of all
   woreda × indicator slots that contained a value; a blank slot is treated as
   *not reported*.) Fewer woredas reported in the later periods, and those that
   did left fewer indicators blank.
5. **Data-entry errors recur in every period.** The count of rows where a
   numerator exceeds its denominator is
   `r paste0(dqx$impossible_num_gt_denom, " (", plabs, ")", collapse = ", ")`.
   These are excluded from every percentage by the pipeline (see the note on the
   100% guardrail below), and they indicate the data-collection template still
   needs the validation built into the recommended fill-in sheet.

## A. Data quality and reporting over time

### Who reported, and how widely

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Mapped woredas reporting per region and period. '—' = the region did not report that period."
include_graphics(fig("T01_participation_matrix.png"))
```

The matrix shows the reporting base contracting. The Oromia row falls from a
high woreda count in the first two periods to a single low value in Wk 28–52,
and Tigray and Central Ethiopia have no entry after Wk 3–15.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Woreda reporting coverage per region across periods (log scale)."
include_graphics(fig("T02_coverage_trend.png"))
```

### Data-quality scorecard

```{r}
dqx |>
  transmute(Period = ifelse(period %in% names(PERIOD_LABELS), PERIOD_LABELS[period], period),
            `Regions` = regions_reporting,
            `Woreda units` = woreda_units,
            `Mapped woredas` = mapped_woredas,
            `Records` = records,
            `% cells filled` = pct_filled,
            `num>denom errors` = impossible_num_gt_denom,
            `raw >100%` = over_100_raw) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Four data-quality dimensions by period."
include_graphics(fig("T03_data_quality_scorecard.png"))
```

The two error columns (`num > denom` and `raw > 100%`) coincide in this data.
Both count the same data-entry mistake, a numerator larger than its denominator,
which arises from a typo or a leaked total row.

::: {.callout-note}
## The 100% guardrail

An earlier version of the single-period report produced regional figures above
100% (for example a timeliness value of 122%). The cause was rows that carried a
numerator without a valid denominator, or a leaked total row whose numerator
exceeded its denominator. The pipeline now applies two rules before computing any
percentage. A woreda contributes to a ratio only when it has both a numerator and
a denominator greater than zero, and for a proportion the numerator must not
exceed the denominator. Rows failing either rule are excluded and logged. The
trends script additionally asserts that no proportion rollup exceeds 100% and
stops the run if one does. Across all three periods the maximum proportion is
exactly 100%.
:::

### Which indicators are chronically left blank

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "National reporting completeness per indicator across periods (share of reporting woredas that filled the indicator)."
include_graphics(fig("T04_reporting_completeness_trend.png"))
```

Timeliness and completeness are filled in almost every woreda in every period.
The preparedness and case-based-reporting indicators are left blank most often.
These indicators are the priorities for follow-up with the regions.

```{r}
nat_tab <- national |>
  filter(value_type == "proportion") |>
  mutate(period = factor(period, levels = periods)) |>
  select(label, period, value_pct) |>
  mutate(value_pct = round(value_pct)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = value_pct) |>
  rename(Indicator = label)

kable(nat_tab, caption = "National KPI value (%) by period.")
```

## How to add the next quarter (reproducible workflow)

The pipeline is designed to extend to additional periods. Adding the next
quarter requires three steps:

1. **Drop the workbooks** into a new folder `raw/<period>/`, e.g.
   `raw/2025-Wk53-65/` (one folder per period; keep the shared
   `All GIS names.xlsx`, `reference_geo_names.csv` and
   `Population by GIS woreda best.xlsx` in the project root).
2. **Add one config block** in `scripts/catalog.R`: copy a `cfg_<period>`
   tribble (file / sheet / header_row / region), `bind_rows` it into
   `REGION_CONFIG`, and append the new label to `PERIOD_LEVELS` /
   `PERIOD_LABELS`.
3. **Rerun** `Rscript scripts/run_all.R`.

What happens automatically:

- the **master** gains the new period (every output carries a `period` column);
- `FOCUS_PERIOD` advances to the newest quarter, so **`kpi_report.qmd` becomes
  the new quarter's standing report** while `run_all.R` archives the previous
  render under its period in `reports/archive/`;
- **this trends report discovers the new period from the data** and extends every
  figure and table — no edits needed here.

See `pipeline_documentation.qmd` for the full developer walkthrough.

---

*Generated from `output/` and `exports/`. Numbers update whenever the pipeline
is rerun. Percentages are `100 × Σ numerator / Σ denominator` over complete
(numerator + valid denominator) pairs.*
